name: Select and Combobox
description: Choosing from a list: the native select for a single choice without search, and a combobox for search, long lists, and several choices, after the APG combobox pattern: focus stays in its input, aria-activedescendant marks the highlighted option, Space types, Enter picks only a highlighted option, and the form sends the chosen value.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing fields win.

layout.layering: A list in the top layer (the popover attribute) needs no z-index. Without it, the list sits with the project's dropdowns and popovers: above page content and sticky bars, below toasts and modals.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Let people choose one or more options from a list. Use the native <select> for a single choice without search; build a combobox (the APG combobox pattern) only when the list needs search, async results, several choices, or rich options. Focus stays in the combobox's input, aria-activedescendant marks the highlighted option, Space types, Enter picks only a highlighted option and never submits the form while the list is open, Escape closes only the list, and a hidden input sends the chosen value with the form. Build on the project's select or combobox component when it has a suitable one. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: The native <select> for a single choice without search, with a placeholder option whose value is empty when it is required
A combobox after the APG pattern for search, async results, several choices, or rich options
Focus stays in the input; aria-activedescendant points to the highlighted option, and nothing is trapped
Space types; Enter picks only a highlighted option and never submits the form while the list is open; Escape closes only the list
The chosen value goes to the form through a hidden input; text that isn't a choice, even only spaces, fails validation; and a form reset brings back the starting choice
Keys that belong to an input method while it composes text are left to it
A select-only combobox for rich options without search, with its own keys: Enter and Space open and pick, and typing letters finds options
Several choices: a multi-select list that stays open, with the chosen values shown outside the input
One status region for results, "No matches", and loading; only the latest search answer counts
The list in the top layer, a highlight with 3:1 contrast, and chosen options marked with a check
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has a select or combobox component, configure or extend it to meet this guide instead of building another one, and keep its API.

2. Choose the variant the task needs (componentSpec.variants): native, searchable, multiple, or selectOnly. Use the native <select> unless the list needs search, async results, several choices, or rich options.
3. For the native select, follow frameworkPatterns.nativeSelect.

4. For a searchable combobox, build the markup and the keys as in frameworkPatterns.searchableCombobox and componentSpec.interactions. For a select-only combobox, follow implementationDetails.selectOnly instead: its keys differ.
5. Add what the variant needs: async results (implementationDetails.asyncOptions), several choices (implementationDetails.multipleChoices), and groups (implementationDetails.groups).
6. Wire required and errors like the project's other fields, and make typed text that isn't a choice fail validation.
7. Show the list in the top layer, and style the highlight and the chosen options (implementationDetails.appearance).
8. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, and a phone, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

componentSpec.goal: Let people choose from a list quickly with a keyboard, a pointer, a touch screen, or a screen reader, without picking or submitting anything by accident.

anatomy.hierarchy: The label names the input and the list. The input (role="combobox") controls the list (role="listbox") of options; a hidden input holds the chosen value. With several choices, the chosen values show as a list outside the input. A status region and the error follow.

slotNotes.label: A visible <label for> on the input; the list is labelled by the same label with aria-labelledby. Required and optional fields say so in words, as other fields do.
slotNotes.input: role="combobox", aria-autocomplete="list", aria-expanded, aria-controls pointing to the list, and aria-activedescendant while an option is highlighted. autocomplete="off", so the browser's own suggestions don't cover the list. The combobox role goes on the input; the popup is always the listbox.
slotNotes.list: role="listbox", hidden while closed, in the top layer (popover) or a portal, so a parent with overflow: hidden can't clip it.
slotNotes.option: role="option" with a unique id and aria-selected; "true" on the chosen option.
slotNotes.groupLabel: A group is an element with role="group", labelled by its heading with aria-labelledby; the heading isn't an option and can't be picked.
slotNotes.value: A hidden input with the field's name holds the chosen option's value, so the form sends the choice, not the typed text. Hidden inputs are left out of constraint validation (checked), so required sits on the visible input, and any text there that isn't a choice, even only spaces, fails with a message such as "Choose a city from the list". A hidden input also can't restore its own value on a form reset, so the combobox keeps the page's starting choice and brings it back, with its text and aria-selected, after a reset that wasn't cancelled.
slotNotes.chosenValues: With several choices: a list of the chosen values outside the input, each with a Remove button named after its value ("Remove Kraków").
slotNotes.status: One status region, present before it changes, for the number of results once typing pauses, "No matches", and loading.
slotNotes.error: Like other fields: in the input's aria-describedby, with aria-invalid while there is an error, and never a live region.

open.description: Whether the list shows; mirrored in aria-expanded on the input.

query.description: The typed text that filters the list. It isn't a choice until an option is picked.

highlighted.description: The index of the highlighted option among the visible ones, or -1 for none; mirrored in aria-activedescendant.

value.description: The chosen value, or values with several choices; sent with the form through hidden inputs with the field's name.

multiple.description: Whether several options can be chosen.

required.description: Whether a choice is needed; required on the visible input.

loading.description: Whether async results are on their way; the status region says "Loading…".

interactions.accessibilityNotes: Typing filters the list and opens it, with nothing highlighted, so Enter can't pick something by accident. Space, Home, End, and letters type and move the caret, as in any text box.

While an input method editor (IME) composes text, such as Japanese, Chinese, or Korean, its keys are its own: the arrows, Enter, and Escape aren't handled. Check isComposing, and keyCode 229, which is how Safari reports the Enter that confirms a composition.
Down and Up open the list and move the highlight, wrapping at the ends; from nothing highlighted, Up goes to the last option. Focus stays in the input.
Picks only a highlighted option; with nothing highlighted, it picks nothing. While the list is open, Enter never submits the form. With the list closed, Enter submits the form as usual.
Closes the list and keeps the text. Cancelling the key keeps a dialog around the combobox open (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). With the list closed, Escape does what it does around it.
Tab closes the list and moves focus on; the typed text isn't a choice unless an option was picked.
Focus stays in the input: cancel mousedown on the list. Cancelling pointerdown instead also stops a tap's click in WebKit (checked).
The list closes, and focus stays where the click put it.

The form puts the input's text back only after its reset event, and a listener after the combobox's can still cancel the reset. So the combobox waits for the event to finish, checks defaultPrevented, and only then restores the page's starting choice: the value, aria-selected, and validity. A cancelled reset keeps the current choice. The same setup runs when the page loads.

responsiveBehavior.layout: The input fills its container; the list is at least as wide as the input (200 px minimum, suggested), below it, or above it when there is no room below.
responsiveBehavior.phones: Text is at least 16 px; options are at least 44 px tall on touch (suggested). The native select opens the phone's own picker.
responsiveBehavior.reflow: At 320 px wide, long option labels wrap, and the list fits the screen.

variants.native: The native <select>: one choice, no search (frameworkPatterns.nativeSelect).
variants.searchable: The APG editable combobox with list autocomplete: typing filters the list (frameworkPatterns.searchableCombobox).
variants.multiple: Several choices: the list has aria-multiselectable="true", picking toggles aria-selected and keeps the list open, and the chosen values show outside the input (implementationDetails.multipleChoices).
variants.selectOnly: Rich options without search: the APG select-only combobox. It has no text box, so its keys differ from the searchable one's (implementationDetails.selectOnly); the list, the value, and the reset work the same way. Where the native select only needs custom styling, appearance: base-select styles it in Chromium (from Chrome 135); other browsers show the standard select.

animations.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the list appears without movement.

requirements.1.3.1: The input is a combobox that controls a listbox of options, and both are named by the visible label.
requirements.1.4.3: Option text meets 4.5:1, highlighted and chosen ones included.
requirements.1.4.11: The input's edge, the highlight, and the focus indicator meet 3:1.
requirements.2.1.1: Everything works from the keyboard: typing, the arrows, Enter, Escape, and Tab.
requirements.2.1.2: Nothing is trapped: Tab always moves on.
requirements.2.4.7: The highlighted option is visible; it is the focus indicator while focus stays in the input.
requirements.2.5.8: Options and Remove buttons are at least 24 px tall.
requirements.3.2.2: Choosing an option doesn't change the page by itself; the choice applies when the form is sent.
requirements.3.3.1: Errors, such as typed text that isn't a choice, are shown in text.
requirements.4.1.2: The combobox exposes its expanded state and active option; options expose their selected state.
requirements.4.1.3: Results, "No matches", and loading are announced through one status region without moving focus.

keyboardNavigation.selectOnly: Its own keys, without a text box: see implementationDetails.selectOnly.
keyboardNavigation.native: The native select keeps the browser's and the platform's own keys.

input.aria-activedescendant: The highlighted option's id, only while one is highlighted

option.aria-selected: "true" on the chosen option, or options

option.aria-disabled: "true" on an option that can't be chosen right now; the arrows skip it
option.aria-setsize and aria-posinset: Only when the list renders part of its options; otherwise browsers count them

screenReader.onFocus: The label, the combobox role, collapsed or expanded, and the current text.
screenReader.highlight: Each highlighted option is read through aria-activedescendant, with its selected state.
screenReader.results: The number of results once typing pauses, and "No matches", through the status region.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version.

nativeSelect.description: A required native select with a placeholder option whose value is empty, and option groups.
nativeSelect.html:
<!-- The first option's empty value is what makes required work: a placeholder
     without value="" counts as a choice. -->
<label for="country">Country</label>
<select id="country" name="country" autocomplete="country" required>
  <option value="">Choose a country</option>
  <optgroup label="Europe">
    <option value="DE">Germany</option>
    <option value="PL">Poland</option>
  </optgroup>
  <optgroup label="Asia">
    <option value="JP">Japan</option>
  </optgroup>
</select>

searchableCombobox.description: A searchable select after the APG editable combobox: filtering, the keys (left to an input method while it composes), the pointer, the hidden input with the chosen value, validity for text that isn't a choice, and the starting choice on load and after a form reset. The longest snippet, since its keys need its state.
searchableCombobox.html:
• Kraków
  • New York
  • Newcastle

implementationDetails.nativeSelect: Give it a <label for>, required when a choice is needed, and autocomplete for personal data, such as country or bday-month. For required to work, the first option is a placeholder with value="" ("Choose a country"); a placeholder without value="" counts as a choice, so the form accepts it (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Group options with <optgroup label>.
implementationDetails.asyncOptions: Ask the server once typing pauses (about 300 ms, suggested), and say "Loading…" in the status region. Answers can arrive out of order, so keep only the latest request's answer: number each request and ignore any other answer, or abort the previous request with an AbortController. "No matches" and errors are text in the popup, not options, and are said in the status region.
implementationDetails.multipleChoices: The list gets aria-multiselectable="true"; picking an option toggles its aria-selected, and the list stays open. The chosen values show outside the input as a list, each with a Remove button named after its value ("Remove Kraków"): interactive elements can't sit inside the input or another button. Each chosen value goes to the form in its own hidden input with the field's name. Optional: Backspace in an empty input removes the last value; say so in the hint.
implementationDetails.groups: In the list, a group is an element with role="group", labelled by its heading with aria-labelledby. The heading isn't an option, and the arrows skip it.

selectOnly.markup: A focusable element (tabindex="0") with role="combobox", named by the visible label with aria-labelledby, with aria-controls, aria-expanded, and aria-activedescendant while the list is open. Its text is the chosen option's text. The list, the hidden input with the value, and the reset work as in the searchable combobox. It isn't a form field, so the form's own validation checks a required choice, and aria-required="true" says it.
selectOnly.closed: Enter, Space, Down Arrow, and Alt+Down Arrow open the list without changing the choice; Up Arrow and Home open it on the first option, and End on the last. Typing letters opens it on the first option that starts with them.
selectOnly.open: Down Arrow and Up Arrow move the highlight, stopping at the ends; Home and End go to the first and last option; Page Up and Page Down jump 10 options. Enter, Space, and Alt+Up Arrow pick the highlighted option and close the list; Tab picks it, closes the list, and moves on; Escape closes the list without changing the choice. Typing letters moves to the first option that starts with them; typing the same letter again moves through the options that start with it.
selectOnly.focus: Focus stays on the combobox, and aria-activedescendant marks the highlighted option, as in the searchable one.
selectOnly.reference: The WAI-ARIA APG select-only combobox example.

implementationDetails.appearance: The highlighted option is the focus indicator, since focus stays in the input: give it at least 3:1 contrast against what's around it, with an outline or a solid background. A faint tint such as #eff6ff on white is 1.1:1. Style the highlight with a class or a data attribute, not :focus, because options never get focus. Chosen options show a check, not color alone. The list opens in the top layer (the popover attribute) or a portal, below the input, or above it when there's no room, with CSS anchor positioning where the project's browsers support it, or the positioning code the project already has.

edgeCases.longLabels: Long option labels wrap; nothing is cut off.
edgeCases.manyOptions: With hundreds of options, filter on the server or render only part of the list; then each option needs aria-setsize and aria-posinset, since browsers can only count rendered options.
edgeCases.disabledOptions: An option that can't be chosen right now has aria-disabled="true", and the arrows skip it.
edgeCases.prefilled: An edit form starts with the chosen option's text in the input and its value in the hidden input. The combobox sets aria-selected and the validity from them when the page loads, and brings them back after a form reset that wasn't cancelled.
edgeCases.inDialog: In a dialog, the first Escape closes the list and the second the dialog.
edgeCases.noScript: Server-rendered pages can start with the native select and replace it with the combobox once the script runs.

must: Build on the project's select or combobox component when it has a suitable one, and keep its API
Use the native select for a single choice without search
Keep focus in the combobox's input, with aria-activedescendant for the highlight
Send the chosen value with the form, not the typed text
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Add a dependency, such as a select or positioning library, without asking
Move focus into the options, or trap focus in the list
Pick an option on Space in a searchable combobox, or on Enter with nothing highlighted
Handle the arrows, Enter, or Escape while an input method composes text
Give a select-only combobox the searchable one's keys
Submit the form on Enter while the list is open
Put buttons or chips inside the input or another button
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: A single choice without search uses the native select, and a required one starts with a placeholder option whose value is empty
The combobox and its list are named by the field's visible label
Typing filters the list without highlighting anything, and Space types a space
The arrow keys move the highlight with aria-activedescendant while focus stays in the input, and the highlight has at least 3:1 contrast
Enter picks only a highlighted option, and never submits the form while the list is open
Escape closes only the list, so a dialog around it stays open
A click or tap on an option picks it and keeps focus in the input, and a click elsewhere closes the list and leaves focus where the click was
The form sends the chosen value, not the typed text, and text that isn't a choice, even only spaces, fails validation with a message
A form reset brings back the starting choice, with its text and its selection, and a cancelled reset keeps the current one
While an input method composes text, the arrows, Enter, and Escape are left to it
A select-only combobox opens with Enter, Space, or the arrows, picks with Enter or Space, and finds options by the letters typed
With several choices, the list stays open, the chosen values show outside the input, and each Remove button names its value
Results, "No matches", and loading are announced through one status region, and an older search answer never replaces a newer one
The list isn't clipped by its container, and works on a phone and at 320 px wide
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens, like its other form controls
